text: Be the one who nurtures and builds. Be the one who has an understanding and a forgiving heart, one who looks for the best in people. Leave people better than you found them.
A true friend is one who not only is willing to love us the way we are, but is able to leave us better than he found us.
source: What Is a Friend? Ensign, Jan. 1973

text: Pleasure usually takes the form of me and now; joy is us and always.
Greatness is best measured by how well an individual responds to the happenings in life that appear to be totally unfair, unreasonable, and undeserved.
Being of good cheer makes it possible for us to turn all of our sunsets into sunrises.
The difference between those who are committed and those who are not is the difference between the words want and will.
Striving can be more important than arriving.
You can never get enough of the things you don't need, because the things you don't need can never satisfy.
True happiness is not made in getting something; true happiness is becoming something.
Tact is rubbing out another's mistakes, not rubbing them in.
Wise is the man who says what needs to be said, but not all that could be said.
Victories in life come through our ability to work around and over the obstacles that cross our path. We grow stronger as we climb our own mountains.
None of us need one more person bashing or pointing out where we have failed or fallen short.
The best and most clear indicator that we are progressing spiritually and coming unto Christ is the way we treat other people.
Real charity is not something you give away; it is something that you acquire and make a part of yourself.
source: Know He Is There, Ensign, Feb. 1994

text: A friend is a possession we earn, not a gift.
source: What Is a Friend? Ensign, Jan. 1973

text: Sometimes when family members least deserve love, they need it most.
If we could look into each other's hearts and understand the unique challenges each of us faces, I think we would treat each other much more gently, with more love, patience, tolerance, and care.

Do not allow yourselves to be made to feel inadequate or frustrated because you cannot do everything others seem to be accomplishing. Only you and your Father in Heaven know your needs, strengths, and desires.
Enduring, or carrying on, is not just a matter of tolerating circumstances and hanging in there, but of pressing forward.
One little lie or dishonest act leads to another until the perpetrator is caught in the web of deceit.
Perhaps the greatest charity comes when we are kind to each other, when we don't judge or categorize someone else, when we simply give each other the benefit of the doubt or remain quiet.
As children of God we are somebody. He will build us, mold us, and magnify us if we will but hold our heads up, our arms out, and walk with him.
Adversity will surface in some form in every life. How we prepare for it, how we meet it, makes the difference. We can be broken by adversity, or we can become stronger.

If we would know true love and understanding one for another, we must realize that communication is more than a sharing of words. It is the wise sharing of emotions, feelings, and concerns. It is the sharing of oneself totally.
One may have many talents and knowledge but never acquire wisdom because he does not learn to be compassionate with his fellow man. We will never approach godliness until we learn to love and lift.
The ultimate maturity is being able to feel and express appreciation promptly, being fully aware of the value and importance, and showing gratitude for it.

If you have self-respect, you will take satisfaction in being well groomed and will not allow yourself to perform shabbily. You will continue to work toward high standards and goals to serve others, to continue and to practice self-discipline. You will not compromise your standards or beliefs.

Charity is accepting someone's differences, weaknesses, and shortcomings; having patience with someone who has let us down; or resisting the impulse to become offended when someone doesn't handle something the way we might have hoped.
A quality person is someone with integrity. To be worthy of the highest trust is a noble attribute and compliment. Certainly it is greater to be trusted than loved.
Soft and small voice communications with our associates make priceless friendships possible.

Good cheer is a state of mind or mood that promotes happiness or joy. With God's help, good cheer permits us to rise above the depressing present or difficult circumstances. It is a process of positive reassurance and reinforcement. It is sunshine when clouds block the light.
Hate is not the opposite of love. Apathy is. We will not have time for apathy in life's journey if we speak and think positively.
Happiness does not depend on what happens outside of you, but on what happens inside of you.
Over the years I have learned that when I need answers to deal with crises, people, and issues, I must go to God.
source: General Conference, Oct. 1988, "The Measure of Our Hearts"

text: Charity is refusing to take advantage of another's weakness and being willing to forgive someone who has hurt us.
We must at regular and appropriate intervals speak and reassure others of our love and the long time it takes to prove it by our actions.
Charity is expecting the best of each other.
Discipline is the bridge between goals and accomplishment.
God becomes more approachable as we look to Him.
Being on time to appointments and meetings is a phase of self-discipline and an evidence of self-respect. Punctuality is a courteous compliment the intelligent person pays to his associates.
Proper communication will always be a main ingredient for building family solidarity and permanence.

Often parents communicate most effectively with their children by the way they listen to and address each other. Their conversations showing gentleness and love are heard by our ever-alert, impressionable children.
Satan is ever present, trying to destroy our glory and remove our crown. One of his most powerful tools is discouragement.
Financial peace of mind is not determined by how much we make, but is dependent upon how much we spend!
How damaging is a habit that permits faultfinding, character assassination, and the sharing of malicious rumors! Gossip and caustic comments often create chains of contention.
Do not doubt your abilities. Do not delay your worthy impressions. With God's help, you cannot fail.
Set your goals—without goals you cannot measure your progress. But don't become frustrated because there are no obvious victories. Remind yourself that striving can be more important than arriving.
A willingness to practice patience. Patience in communication is that certain ingredient of conduct we hope others will exhibit toward us when we fail to measure up.
Punctuality or the lack thereof oftentimes is the only introduction one will ever have to new groups and friends.
God knows the feelings in every human heart. He can soften sorrow and lead when there seems to be no light. Prayer can give guidance and confidence.
Progression and achievement belong to those who have learned to use the opportunity of now. Our strides of today will determine our locations tomorrow.
In times of hurt and discouragement, it may be consoling for all of us to recall that no one can do anything permanently to us that will last for eternity.
God's love for us is constant and will not diminish, but he cannot rescue us from the painful results that are caused by wrong choices.
The direction in which we are moving is more important than where we are at the moment. Goal setting should cause us to stretch as we make our way.
Constant criticism can wear one down and weaken knees.

Sometimes when family members least deserve love, they need it most. Love is not appropriately expressed in threats, accusations, expressions of disappointment, or retaliation. Real love takes time, patience, help, and continuing performances.
Day-to-day acts of service, whether for good or evil, may not seem important, but they are building cords of love that become so strong they can seldom be broken.
There is a great need today for all mankind to heed the plea to cease to find fault one with another.
A truly wise person will constantly move forward, striving for self-improvement, knowing that daily repentance is needed for progress.
Procrastination is a deadly weapon of human progress.

The world is filled with too many of us who are inclined to indicate our love with an announcement or declaration. True love is a process. True love requires personal action. Love must be continuing to be real. Love takes time.
It is up to each of us to search for and build upon the gifts which God has given. We must remember that each of us is made in the image of God, that there are no unimportant persons.
Resentment and anger are not good for the soul. They are foul things.
Where you have been is not nearly as important as where you are and where you're going.
Leaders on every level should be primarily interested in rendering compassionate caring for others.
God grant to all of us the power and strength to be people of integrity, and the insight and wisdom to avoid being led into the snares of the dishonest.
All of us need to be constantly reminded it takes a heap of living and loving to make a house a home.
Someone has said, "A friend is a person who is willing to take me the way I am." May I quickly suggest that we are something less than a real friend if we leave a person the same way we find him.
source: What Is a Friend? Ensign, Jan. 1973

text: Worthiness is a process, and perfection is an eternal trek. We can be worthy to enjoy certain privileges without being perfect.
Adaptability cushions the impact of change or disappointment.
Peace is a blessing that comes to those who trust in God. It is established through individual righteousness.

A quality person is someone with integrity. To be worthy of the highest trust is a noble attribute and compliment. Certainly it is greater to be trusted than loved. Truly happy persons will always be totally honest in their dealings with their fellowman.
The family as an institution today is beset on all sides. Conflicts within the family are critical and often damaging.
Lying damages others. Lying subtly permits us to destroy ourselves as we are caught in the snare and shatter our own self-image and credibility.
It is a happy day when we come to know that with God's help, nothing is impossible for us.
You owe it to yourself to keep fit. No matter how busy or how involved you are, you should have some type of physical program to keep the body in tune.
A friend in the true sense is not a person who passively nods approval of our conduct or ignores improper behavior. A friend is a person who cares.
source: What Is a Friend? Ensign, Jan. 1973

text: Some think the only way to get even, to get attention or advantage, or to win is to bash people. This kind of behavior is never appropriate.
We invite all to serve the Savior and walk in His paths straightway. There is an urgency for all of us who have this knowledge of His divinity to act upon it without hesitation or delay.
Peace—not passion, not personal possessions, not personal accomplishments nor happiness—is one of the greatest blessings a man can receive.
Blessed is he or she who avoids being offended.
How comfortable some of us become as we nestle in the web of procrastination. It is a false haven of rest for those who are content to live without purpose, commitment, or self-discipline.
We should teach, particularly ourselves, that nobody is a nobody. We are someone, and with God's help we can accomplish all things.
We are poor in character when we think getting by is a substitute for doing our best.
Difficulties can be a valuable tool in our pursuit of perfection. Adversity need have no necessary connection with failure.
It is not so important whether a young man has been through the experience of a mission as it is whether the mission experience has been through him.
Many marriage tragedies are caused, not by lack of money, but rather by the mismanagement of it.
The gospel is one of harmony, unity, and agreement. It must be presented in love, and with glad tidings, by those who are calm.
Soft and small voice communications with our associates make priceless friendships possible. I am appreciative of people who find no need to raise their voices as they try to impress or convince.
What we are is more important than what we have or what is said of us.
Controversy and contention are weakening habits. Anger is a poor substitute for self-mastery and compassionate service.
Each of us has the challenge to know the Father and to become one with Him.
Ugly reports and conversations are always available to those who would promote the sordid and sensational. None of us are yet perfect.
We need to remove unworthy from our vocabulary and replace it with hope and work.
A man must rise by his own efforts and walk by faith.
Through microscopic examination one can find in almost every life incidents or traits that can be destructive when they are magnified.
One who practices pure religion soon discovers it is more rewarding to lift a man up than to hold him down.
Someone has wisely stated that hate is not the opposite of love. Apathy is. Seek, search, and work for worthy eternal qualities and friends.

How often have we ourselves said or have heard others exclaim in times of crisis or trouble, 'I just don't know where to turn'? There is a gift available to all of us—the gift of looking to God for direction.
Our capacity to see and comprehend is increased only in proportion to our willingness to look.
